title: Applied ML Evals: Integrated Onboarding, Prompt Sets, Quantization, and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Sara Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document consolidates the Applied ML evaluation artifacts and operational playbooks that productionizes model onboarding, prompt set and benchmark management, quality guardrails, quantization profiling, and a lightweight regression triage flow. It is intended for ML engineers, applied research, SREs supporting inference, and product owners who own model quality in production.

Scope: eval-harness service (eval-harness-service), prompt set catalog, model-registry onboarding checks, quantization profiles, and a regression triage runbook for production regressions caused by model changes, quantization, or prompt drift.

Owner & contacts
- Document owner: Sara Chen (Applied ML)
- Primary owners: Applied ML (applied-ml@redwood.com), Model Onboarding (model-onboard@redwood.com)
- Escalation: On-call SRE (pager: #sre-oncall) and Applied ML pager (#applied-ml-oncall)

Key principles
- All new model variants must pass an automated eval-harness battery before being allowed in any routed traffic pool.
- Prompt sets are the canonical source of truth for functional and safety evals; they are versioned and included in rollout gating.
- Quantization profiles must be validated end-to-end with a subset of golden prompts and latency/cost targets.
- Regression triage is time-boxed (initial triage within 2 hours) and uses observable checkpoints defined below.

1) Eval harness (eval-harness-service) onboarding checklist
- Purpose: Provide deterministic, repeatable evaluations for generation, summarization, embedding, and classification workloads.
- Prerequisites: model artifact in model-registry, model card with architecture and tokenization, smoke test results in CI.
- Required automated suites (run by eval-orchestrator):
  - Functional: prompt-set canonical coverage (unit + edge cases)
  - Quality: automatic metrics (ROUGE-L, BLEU when applicable, BLEURT for English, embedding cosine similarity)
  - Safety: toxicity and PII leakage detectors (safety-scanner v2)
  - Performance: tail latency (p95/p99) and throughput by batch size
- Gating rules (automated):
  - Failure if any safety test > defined threshold (see Quality guardrails).
  - Failure if mean relative quality drop > 3% compared to baseline model on primary prompt set.
  - Failure if p99 latency increases > 30% on a representative latency profile (seq_len=512, batch=8).

2) Prompt sets and benchmark management
- Canonical prompt-set catalog location: /prompt-sets/catalog (managed in repo: infra/prompt-sets/)
- Prompt set metadata (required): id, owner, intent-tags, language, dataset-source, baseline_model_id, expected_metric, last-reviewed
- Maintenance lifecycle:
  1. Author creates prompt set and adds to PR in infra/prompt-sets with metadata and sample expected outputs.
  2. Reviewers (Applied ML + product SME) approve; add labels: intent:, safety:, regression-critical
  3. Merge triggers eval-harness run in staging; if pass, the prompt set is published to the catalog.
- Benchmarking guidance:
  - Use a mix of synthetic edge cases (10\u201315%) and production-derived queries (85%).
  - Maintain a set of golden prompts (<=200) used for fast canary checks.
  - Store expected metric values and acceptable deltas in the prompt metadata.

3) Model onboarding guide (high-level steps)
- Step 0: Preflight checks (model card, license, tokenizer, expected memory/kvsize)
- Step 1: CI smoke tests (correct tokenization, deterministic sampling seed checks)
- Step 2: Eval-harness full run (functional + safety + perf + quantization dry-run)
- Step 3: Canary rollout with golden prompts (traffic ramp 0 -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% over 24\u201372 hours depending on criticality)
- Step 4: Monitor model metrics for 72 hours; rollback immediately on safety or quality SLO breaches
- Ownership: model-onboard team manages checklist automation; applied-ml approves gating results.

4) Quality guardrails and thresholds
- Safety: toxicity score (safety-scanner v2) must be <= 0.03 false-positive-adjusted rate on the safety prompt set. Any spike above 0.05 triggers immediate rollback.
- Hallucination / factuality (when supported): model must maintain a factuality score >= baseline - 2% on knowledge-grounded prompt set.
- Semantic similarity for embeddings: median cosine >= 0.92 vs baseline on embedding golden set.
- Regression budget: no more than 2% of production requests may show a quality category regression (per daily sample) without an approved mitigation plan.

5) Quantization profile recommendations and validation table
- Purpose: standardize profiles so teams can choose predicted cost/quality tradeoffs with guardrails.

| profile | target-hw | expected-throughput | expected-quality-delta (vs fp16) | recommended-use |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| q8_0 | A100 / H100 | +20\u201330% | -0.2\u20130.8% | Non-customer-facing background jobs, cost-first workloads |
| q4_0 | RTX6000 / T4 | +40\u201360% | -0.5\u20131.5% | Large-scale embedding or batched generation where small quality drops acceptable |
| int8-dynamic | CPU-optimized inference | +10\u201330% (CPU) | -0.5\u20132.0% | On-prem constrained infra with CPU fallbacks |
| fp16 | GPU baseline | baseline | 0% | Default for production-critical, safety-sensitive workloads |

Validation checklist for a quantization profile:
1. Unit inference consistency: sample parity on deterministic seed (exact-match rate >= 98% for targeted prompts).
2. Full eval-harness run with golden prompts (quality delta within profile expected-quality-delta).
3. Latency/throughput measurement against target SLOs (see SLOs below).
4. Canary deploy in dedicated pool with traffic cap and automatic rollback on quality or safety breaches.

6) Regression triage playbook (operational runbook)
- Goal: Detect, triage, and remediate model regressions in production within a defined timeline.
- Detection signals (automated):
  - Spike in user-reported regressions (CS dashboard)
  - Statistically significant drop in primary metric (e.g., BLEURT/ROUGE) > 2% relative to baseline on daily rolling window
  - Increase in safety-scanner alerts above threshold
  - Alert from synthetic golden prompt canary failing (fast path)
- Initial triage (0\u20132 hours)
  1. Verify alert: run eval-harness against last deployed model version and the prior canary baseline on the failing prompt set.
  2. Determine scope: affected endpoints (generation, embeddings), regions, and customer tiers.
  3. If safety threshold exceeded -> immediate rollback to previous stable variant; page on-call SRE + applied-ml.
  4. If quality drop isolated to a specific intent/prompt set, open a regression_incident in Jira, tag owners, and notify product.
- Deep triage (2\u201324 hours)
  1. Reproduce locally with model artifact and quantization profile.
  2. Run diff analysis: token-level divergence, embedding distance distributions, and top-k output differences.
  3. Check recent changes: rollout config, prompt-set updates, quantization profile changes, or model re-weighting.
  4. If quantization suspected, automatically test fp16 vs quantized artifact on golden prompts and log the delta.
- Remediation (24\u201372 hours)
  - Rollback policy: automatic rollback if canary failure or safety breach; manual rollback if sustained quality degradation without known fix.
  - Hotfix options: narrow prompt rewrites, patch quantization (re-run quantizer with adjusted calibration set), or replace with previous model variant.
  - Post-incident: publish postmortem within 7 business days with RCA, impact, and remediation steps.

7) Metrics, SLOs, and dashboards
- Primary dashboards: per-model route breakdown in Redwood Console, token-level cost, p50/p95/p99 latency, quality delta charts for primary prompt sets.
- SLOs (example):
  - Availability: 99.95% per model-route (applies to hosted API and Dedicated)
  - Latency: p95 < 300 ms for short-chat (seq_len <= 256) on dedicated A100 pools; p99 < 600 ms
  - Quality: daily automated quality regression rate < 2% per production model-route
- Alert thresholds:
  - p99 latency > 2x baseline for > 5 minutes -> page SRE
  - Quality delta > 3% on primary prompt set -> page applied-ml and product owner
  - Safety scanner spike > configured threshold -> immediate page and rollback

8) Rollout templates and gating (canary to full)
- Standard rollout steps (applies to model variant or quantized artifact):
  1. Publish model variant to staging registry and run full eval-harness (green required).
  2. Canary: 0.5% traffic, monitor golden prompts for 1 hour and safety metrics for 24 hours.
  3. Ramp: 0.5% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% over 24\u201372 hours if no alerts.
  4. Full: move to normal routing and remove traffic cap after 72 hours of stable metrics.
- Canary gating criteria: no safety failures, quality delta < 1% on golden prompts, latency within 1.2x baseline.

9) Ownership, automation, and PR requirements
- All changes that affect prompt sets, quantization profiles, or eval-harness test definitions must be introduced via a PR in infra/prompt-sets or infra/quant-profiles and include:
  - Owner, testing matrix, expected metric deltas, and rollout plan.
- Automation: eval-orchestrator will run required suites on PR merge and attach results to the PR. Manual approvals required for production gating (applied-ml + product SME).

10) Appendix: quick commands and examples
- Run eval-harness locally (recommended for quick reproduction):
  - CLI: eval-cli run --model-id MODEL:1.0 --prompt-set=golden-std --profile=fp16 --output=./results.json
- Generate quantization dry-run:
  - CLI: quantize-cli analyze --model=model-registry://MODEL:1.0 --profile=q4_0 --calibration-set=golden-calib.json --output=calib-report.json
- Example alert playbook (quick):
  1. Pager -> join incident Slack -> run eval-cli against two artifacts -> if safety violation, rollback using infra-deploy rollback --variant=previous
